Malavaggo

250 For whom this <note>the root of evil</note> is cut off, uprooted, and removed, he indeed attains concentration <note>original: "samādhi"</note> by day or by night.
8 The Story of the Young Tissa, III 357

251 There is no fire like lust, there is no grip like hatred, there is no net like delusion, there is no river like craving.
9 The Story of the Five Lay-followers, III 360

252 The faults of others are easy to see, but one's own are difficult to see. A person winnows the faults of others like chaff, but covers his own faults like a deceitful gambler hiding a losing die <note>original: "kaliṃ"</note>.
10 The Story of Meṇḍakasetthi, III 363

253 For one who is always looking at the faults of others and who is always censorious, his corruptions <note>original: "āsavā"</note> increase; he is far from the destruction of corruptions.
11 The Story of the Monk Ujjhānasaññī, III 376

254 There is no track in the sky, there is no recluse <note>original: "samaṇo"</note> outside <note>i.e., outside the Buddha's teaching</note>. Mankind delights in complications <note>original: "papañcābhiratā"</note>, but the Tathāgatas are free from complications.

255 There is no track in the sky, there is no recluse outside. There are no eternal compounded things <note>original: "saṅkhārā"</note>, there is no wavering for the Buddhas.
12 The Story of the Wanderer Subhadda, III 377

XVIII THE CHAPTER ON IMPURITIES (MALAVAGGO), THE EIGHTEENTH

---

1 In the Bʳ manuscript: kaḷi va; 2 In the F manuscript: ca; In the Bʳ manuscript: va
3 In the K and F manuscripts: bāhiro; In the Bʳ and Sᵉ manuscripts: bāhire

252 Jātaka, III 223

<summary>This page contains verses 250 through 255 of the Malavaggo (Chapter on Impurities) from the Dhammapada, focusing on the removal of mental defilements, the danger of focusing on the faults of others, and the nature of the enlightened Tathāgata.</summary>
<keywords>Dhammapada, Malavaggo, lust, hatred, delusion, craving, faults, Tathāgata, recluses, compounded things</keywords>
